title: Overdue Draw Charges on Reconstruction Contracts
content:
An overdue draw charge is posted on a past-due customer-funded draw of a Reconstruction contract, one charge per calendar month fee period.

## Scope

For the overdue draw charge on the contract's most recently requested customer-funded draw, the one with the highest draw number among the customer-funded draws, when every earlier customer-funded draw of the contract is paid in full, so that it is the oldest unpaid customer-funded draw, and only for that draw, the charge for a fee period is worked out under the overdue draw charge rules. A charge on any other draw is the tier's monthly overdue percentage of the draw's unpaid amount, at most once per draw per calendar month fee period, rounded to the cent, half up, as the base overdue rule states, except that on a Texas property, until the Texas statutory retention days after the substantial completion date have passed, the unpaid amount of a customer-funded draw leaves out its statutory retention, so a Texas customer-funded draw that has everything but its statutory retention paid carries no overdue draw charge in that time.

## When the charge is fixed

The overdue draw charge for a fee period is not fixed until no deductive change order proposal stands on the contract awaiting the customer's signature; a deductive proposal whose credit worked out under the deductive change order signature rule is nothing is not counted, because it cannot be written.

Read against the contract's records on the charge date: while a deductive change order proposal stands on the contract awaiting the customer's signature, the charge for the fee period is not yet fixed; a deductive proposal whose credit worked out under the deductive change order signature rule is nothing does not count.

## Fee periods

The fee periods of a draw are calendar months: a charge is owed for each calendar month that has begun, from the month that contains the first day a charge may post (the day after the grace period's last day) onward, at most one charge per month, and the charge worked out under these rules is the one for the earliest owed month that carries no charge on the draw yet, written as that month in YYYY-MM form.

A fee period owes no overdue draw charge, and no charge is recorded for it, when the charge worked out for it comes to less than half a cent.

**Illustration (hypothetical dates).** A draw whose first chargeable day falls on the 27th of March owes a fee period for March; on the 4th of May it also owes April and May. If only March carries a charge, the next charge worked out is the one for April, written as that year's April in YYYY-MM form.

## Invocation: `post_overdue_draw_charge_f6859441`

`post_overdue_draw_charge_f6859441` is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks it and then calls it. One call posts an overdue draw charge for one monthly fee period on a past-due draw: it adds one overdue draw charge line, dated today, naming the draw and the fee period and carrying the charge amount, and raises the contract balance by the same amount. Afterwards the charge appears among the contract's charges and the contract balance is higher by the charge.

### Parameters

- `rebuild_contract_id` — the reference number of the Reconstruction contract, as returned by the contract lookup.
- `rebuild_draw_id` — the reference number of the overdue draw the charge is assessed on, as returned by the draw lookup for that contract.
- `fee_period` — the calendar month fee period the charge is for, written YYYY-MM.
- `amount` — the charge amount in US dollars, a number with exactly 2 decimal places; any further digits are rounded to the cent, half up.

### Return

A one-line confirmation naming the new charge line reference (a text id beginning "rbo_"), the draw reference, the fee period, the charge amount in US dollars with 2 decimals and the new contract balance in US dollars with 2 decimals. The presence of the charge line reference means the charge was posted.
